tasks.spec:
You are a read-only design reviewer for a LIVE patient-facing SMS booking pathway. Your working directory contains ./source (read-only material) and you may write EXACTLY ONE file: ./report.md. Never modify anything under ./source, never write any other file, never run destructive commands, do not load skills or call MCP/Apps, and make no network calls.

THE SYSTEM. ./source/CONTEXT.md explains the whole job — read it first. ./source/v61_graph.json is the live Bland SMS pathway (41 nodes, 111 edges) that texts Mott Optical recall patients and books one eye exam at the MK2 office. ./source/build_v61.py generates it; ./source/scenarios.py is the 30-scenario suite; ./source/check_candidate_gate.py is the deterministic gate; ./source/redproof_run.py proves the gate catches rule removals.

THE JOB. Ankit is changing the pathway (v62): (1) the post-booking close must end, verbatim: "You're all set. If you have further questions, please call MK2 Optical at (212) 219-2219"; (2) any patient request AFTER booking — later in the same thread, or texting back into a finished thread — gets, verbatim: "For that you'll have to contact the MK2 Optical office at (212) 219-2219"; (3) locked decisions: (212) 219-2219 replaces (855) 750-6688 in ALL ELEVEN nodes that carry it, and the deferral applies POST-BOOKING ONLY — the pre-booking steer-back loops in n_office and n_faq keep their behavior with the new number.

YOUR EMPHASIS (the other reviewers have different ones): the patient experience and copy integrity — read every changed line as the patient will receive it on a phone. Where does the mandated copy collide with the existing warmth, bilingual rules, or tone? When a booked patient texts back "thanks" or a question, what exact message sequence do they get under your design, and does it ever read as cold, duplicated, or contradictory? Does any path let a patient see two different phone numbers or two different practice names in one thread?

WRITE ./report.md WITH THESE SECTIONS (any reasonable headings):
1. CHANGE LIST — every node whose copy or routing changes for v62. Cover at least: n_confirm, n_office, n_faq, e_safe_identity, e_safe_failure, e_booking_failed, e_office, e_declined, e_stop, e_not_me, e_existing (the eleven carrying (855) 750-6688), plus e_booked and n_identity. For each: quote the current patient-visible line, give the exact proposed line, note prompt-rule side effects (language rules, NO_CLAIM, NO_LEAK).
2. COME-BACK DESIGN — how a patient texting back into a finished thread gets the deferral line. Ground it in Bland mechanics (isStart node, new_conversation sends, End Call semantics, inbound routing). Bland's post-End-Call inbound behavior is UNMEASURED: name the empirical probe(s) that settle it, and show your design works or fails safe under each plausible behavior. Weigh gateway extension (adding a booked flag to /patient-search) against Bland-only alternatives; recommend one.
3. SCENARIO ADDITIONS — new scenarios.py entries (name each, with expected node/outcome), minimum: post-booked extra ask, text-back after close, and the cases your design creates.
4. GATE AND REDPROOF ADDITIONS — deterministic rules for check_candidate_gate.py (e.g., zero occurrences of the old number, mandated lines present verbatim where required) and the redproof mutations proving each rule can catch a removal.
5. REGRESSION RISKS — what this change can break, explicitly including the NO_CLAIM rule, the never-rebook-after-success guard, bilingual switching, and STOP/wrong-person suppression. Flag the Mott Optical vs MK2 Optical brand inconsistency (26 nodes say Mott Optical) and recommend one naming, marked as Ankit's call.

HONESTY RULES. Quote only text that actually exists in ./source files. If something is unknowable from the material, say unknown — never invent Bland behavior. Keep it under 3000 words: decisions and evidence, not restatement.
tasks.verified: report.md covers all 13 required nodes, both mandated lines verbatim, come-back mechanics grounded in Bland semantics with a named empirical probe, scenario/gate/redproof additions, regression risks, and the brand-naming flag.
